items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Same when I worked with Hank Crawford you know.

ctx.x: I read something about when you had the publication, the Tribe publication and you had used the word “relegate.” You have to learn how to relegate some things or you’re going to lose your mind.

Yeah. You have to get help or expedite you know, the different responsibilities. Because I’m a saxophone player. I’m chasing notes, you know what I mean? And you know in this quest of playing the saxophone and dealing with the jazz language you know, I have to call on different other avenues of like in media, publishing, people that is an expert in that particular area and have skills in that particular area. I had to like actually create a network of, create a network of — like Eddie Harris would say, create an…

sergeants that can help. Because he was very — of course the great Eddie Harris — we were very close. We recorded and toured together for a long time. And every city Eddie would have, he would call a sergeant or a help in every state, city and state, he would have people helping him dealing with concerts and workshops, and so it was easy for him when every time he would tour he would get many big engagements from big agencies out of New York but he would always call on these people in these cities to help set up…
